import java.util.Scanner;
import java.io.PrintStream;

public class Main {
    private static final long MOD = 1000000007L;

    private static long fastPow(long a, long p) {
        long res = 1;
        long base = a % MOD;
        long exp = p;
        while (exp > 0) {
            if ((exp & 1) == 1) {
                res = (res * base) % MOD;
            }
            base = (base * base) % MOD;
            exp >>= 1;
        }
        return res;
    }

    private static boolean solve(Scanner scanner, PrintStream out, boolean multipleTestMode) {
        if (!scanner.hasNextLong()) {
            return false;
        }
        long p = scanner.nextLong();
        if (!scanner.hasNextLong()) {
            return false;
        }
        long k = scanner.nextLong();

        if (multipleTestMode && !scanner.hasNextLong()) {
            // In multiple test mode, if we cannot read more, we still process this test
            // but the C++ code returns false only if ist fails after reading p and k? Actually it reads p and k, then checks if multipleTestMode && !ist. Since we already read successfully, we don't return false here.
            // The C++ code: if (multipleTestMode && !ist) return false; after reading p and k. But ist is the stream, after reading p and k, if the stream is in fail state, it returns false. In Java, if we successfully read two longs, the scanner is not in error state. So we don't need to check again.
        }

        // Debug print (optional, we can skip)
        // System.err.println("Next test: " + p + " " + k);

        if (k == 0) {
            long ans = fastPow(p, p - 1);
            out.println(ans);
            return multipleTestMode;
        }

        if (k == 1) {
            long ans = fastPow(p, p);
            out.println(ans);
            return multipleTestMode;
        }

        long groups = 0;
        boolean[] used = new boolean[(int)(p + 1)]; // p is small enough for array
        long ans = 1;

        for (long x = 1; x < p; ++x) {
            int idx = (int)x;
            if (used[idx]) continue;

            ++groups;
            ans = (ans * p) % MOD;

            used[idx] = true;
            long v = x;
            while (true) {
                v = (v * k) % p;
                int vidx = (int)v;
                if (used[vidx]) break;
                used[vidx] = true;
            }
        }

        out.println(ans);
        return multipleTestMode;
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
        PrintStream out = System.out;

        // In the original code, if not ONLINE_JUDGE, it loops while solve returns true.
        // Since we are not defining ONLINE_JUDGE, we will loop until EOF.
        while (solve(scanner, out, true)) {
            // continue
        }
    }
}
